newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish to issue bonds worth $500 mln abroad in '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish to issue bonds worth $500 mln abroad in '97.

text.p: Poland will probably use all the $500 million allotted for international debt market issues in next year's budget, a deputy finance minister said.
"We presently believe that we will use the whole amount," Krzysztof Kalicki told Reuters.
Earlier on Wednesday the government increased the upper limit for budget financing on international markets in the 1997 draft budget to $500 million from $300 million.
Kalicki said the time and denomination of next year's issues would depend on market conditions but added that Poland was interested in Yankee and Samurai bonds.
"We are continuing work on an American market issue and we are also talking about yen-denominated bonds," Kalicki said.

Poland returned to international finance markets in 1995 with a $250 million issue, followed this year with a 250 million German mark five-year eurobond priced at 65 basis points above comparable bunds.
Kalicki also said Poland was planning to borrow $87.5 million from foreign branches of Polish banks next year. @
Poland's rating by Moody's Investor Service is now Baa3, while that of Standard and Poor's is BBB-.
